title: Heating Up, Backing Down: Evaluating recent climate policy progress in Canada
field_subject: subject:Climate change|subject:Climate change policies|subject:Carbon price|subject:Emission trading|subject:Public policy|subject:Provincial climate change policies|subject:Fossil fuels
field_description: The report assesses the climate policy progress regarding GHG emissions reductions, summarizing policies of the federal government and each of the provinces over the past two years. The report identifies two important issues in Canadian climate policy: an overemphasis on carbon pricing and an absence of supply-side energy policies. Building on the 2017 report Tracking Progress: Evaluating government plans and actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in Canada, Mertins-Kirkwood analyzes new emissions data and new policy announcements to assess federal, provincial and territorial governments’ progress toward Canada’s domestic and international greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction targets. He concludes that positive progress in British Columbia and Quebec is outweighed by backsliding in other provinces, and future progress is further threatened by the legislative reversals enacted by the recently-elected conservative governments in Alberta and Ontario, which are Canada’s two biggest carbon polluting provinces.
